To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a 500 MHz to ~2.5 GHz push-pull power amp was designed, fabricated and tested.
a broadband high PAE GaAs push-pull power amp was designed, fabricated, and tested.
a 20 W, 500 MHz to ~2.5 GHz, broadband, high power-added efficiency GaN push-pul power amplifier is presented.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, fabrication, and testing of high power microwave amplifiers.
the design of broadband high power-added efficiency (PAE), push-pull power amplifiers for applications such as military communications, radar, and commercial applications.
developing a high efficiency, broadband power amplifier for radar applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paper is very well written, and the authors should be congratulated on a very fine piece of work.
this work has shown the feasibility of achieving high power added efficiency in a broadband GaN push-pul power amplifier.
the push-pull configuration is the most suitable topology to be employed in broadband high efficiency amplifiers, especially in the 500MHz-2.5GHz frequency range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the push-pull amplifier design is a viable solution for achieving broadband power amplifier operation.
the GaN push-pulldesign is a viable alternative to the GaN single-ended design for broadband applications.
the GaN push-pul amplifier with 47% PAE from 500 MHz-2.5GHz is the highest efficiency GaN PA over such wide frequency range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the power added efficiency is not limited to the 25Ω load line and can be increased with the addition of reactive matching.
a broadband high efficiency power amplifier can be designed using GaN ICs without any reactive matching.
broadband operation can be achieved with GaN ICs and a broadband balun without the need for a distributed power amplifier design.
